title: Surge-sensing soft-pinning and token-budget shedding playbook for multi-region routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define and implement a multi-region routing policy that senses short-term regional surges and applies soft-pinning + prioritized token-budget shedding per model tier. This is intended to protect SLOs (p50/p95 latency and availability) while maximizing request success and preserving affinity when capacity recovers. The feature should be compatible with existing steering/weights config and expose conservative knobs for Dedicated and Hosted customers.

Background: Recent incidents (see links) showed that hard geo-ejection causes large cache invalidation spikes and a cascade of latency regressions when traffic shifts back. We need a gentler mechanism that both preserves locality for cached KV prefixes and can shed load predictably when regional GPU pools saturate. We also want a per-model token-budget shed policy to avoid starving high-value, short requests when queues grow.

Scope: Implement runtime + control-plane pieces: surge detector (short-term capacity headroom + latency delta), soft-pin decision function, per-request steering p-score computation, token-budget shedding controller, and a region-level circuit-breaker with draining state. Work will include runtime changes (routing/steering libs), config schema in control plane, console UI for visualizing soft-pinned flows, and automated canary + chaos testing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Surge detector emits explicit events for region R when GPU headroom < configured threshold AND p95 latency delta > threshold for 20s
2) Soft-pin preserves affinity: at least 60% of traffic for pinned customers stays in preferred region when downstream capacity has >15% headroom
3) Token-budget shedding kicks in when region queue length exceeds N and ensures high-priority models retain 80% of tokens compared to baseline
4) Region circuit-breaker transitions: CLOSED -> SOFT-DRAIN -> OPEN and back according to documented hysteresis and custody checks
5) No regressions in unit test suite; end-to-end canary with synthetic traffic reproduces expected shedding and recovery behavior
6) Console shows per-region soft-pin ratio + shed counts and customers can opt-out via route config
design_notes: We favor a probabilistic soft-pin rather than hard pinning to avoid cold-KV cache storms. Soft-pin score = affinity_weight * affinity_score + capacity_factor * (1 - utilization). Affinity_score uses persistent routing hints (customer preference, IP locality, previous successful region). capacity_factor uses GPU util + queued_work normalized per instance type. We will expose two main knobs: soft_pin_aggressiveness (0..1) and token_budget_cut (percentage per model-tier).
tradeoffs_decision: After prototyping both hard-eject and soft-probabilistic approaches, we chose soft-probabilistic pinning. Tradeoffs: soft-pinning keeps cache warm and smooths user experience but can delay capacity relief during extreme overload. To mitigate, we combine soft-pinning with token-budget shedding that targets low-value/background models first and a short SOFT-DRAIN window before OPEN state to allow graceful KV eviction if needed.
implementation_plan: A) Runtime: implement surge_detector metrics collector and steering plugin (Marco) - 2 points
B) Control plane: add soft_pin config + token_budget rules UI (Lina) - 1.5 points
C) Console: charts and toggles for soft-pin + per-route opt-outs (Evan) - 1 point
D) E2E: chaos test harness and canary (SRE) - 0.5 points
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring function, integration tests with simulated multi-region clusters, and a chaos experiment that injects 3x request surge in a single region for 5 minutes. Canary rollout will be done to 10% of traffic with detailed tracing enabled. Expected canary windows: 24h for Hosted API, staged rollout to Dedicated customers after validation.
metrics_and_slos: Primary SLOs impacted: p50 latency (<80ms), p95 latency (<250ms), success rate (>99.5%). New metrics: region_soft_pin_ratio, region_surge_events, token_shed_count_by_model_tier, region_circuit_state, region_queue_length. Alerts: surge_event sustained 30s -> pager if customer_impact=high and success_rate drops >0.5%.
rollback_plan: Disable soft_pin via control plane flag and revert steering plugin to existing weighted routing. If token-budget shedding causes customer impact, revert to baseline token allocations and open an incident. All changes are feature-flagged behind 'surge_softpin_v1'.

2026-03-05 - Marco Chen: Bench results from simulator attached. Soft-pin reduced cross-region ejection events by ~72% and avoided large KV misses; overall p95 improved under moderate surges but under extreme 10x surges token-shed was required to hold success rate.
